patterns.title: Bounded Work
patterns.summary: Split large work into resumable units and limit the resources consumed in one scheduling turn.

patterns.title: Continuous Batching
patterns.summary: Rebuild shared execution work at safe boundaries as requests arrive, advance, and finish.

patterns.title: Memory Indirection
patterns.summary: Separate logical positions from reusable physical storage through an explicit mapping layer.

patterns.title: Overload and Backpressure
patterns.summary: Bound queued work and define an explicit action when a producer outruns a constrained consumer or resource.

patterns.title: Ownership and Background Work
patterns.summary: Move work off the control path without creating two authoritative owners of mutable state.

patterns.title: Online Repartitioning
patterns.summary: Move live partition ownership through explicit transitional states while preserving one write authority and every acknowledged mutation.

patterns.title: Prefix Reuse
patterns.summary: Index and retain reusable computation for the longest semantically valid shared request prefix.

patterns.title: Speculative Execution
patterns.summary: Perform cheap tentative work, verify it against an authority, and commit only accepted results.

patterns.title: Approximation Contracts
patterns.summary: Trade exact work for bounded resources only after defining an oracle, an error metric, and an operational envelope.

patterns.title: Atomic Generation Replacement
patterns.summary: Build replacement state away from readers and publish one complete, validated generation through an atomic authority switch.

patterns.title: Cross-System Atomicity
patterns.summary: Represent multi-system side effects as recoverable, idempotent state transitions when no shared transaction exists.
